title: A Turn off can replace an opt-in another device turned on while its cancel was out
evidence: Done 2026-11-14: cancelReminders (widget-src/standalone/reminders.ts) reads the opt-in again after postCancel answers; if it is no longer the same opt-in (sameOptIn: status, token, provider), the later decision stands, and nothing is written or counted (US-17 AC17). Option A of the design note. Tests: standalone/reminders-cancel-superseded.test.ts (the real store over MemoryCloud; fails on main: expected 'cancelled' to be 'active') and the US-17 AC17 table in reminders.test.ts. Residual (US-17 AC17 Limit): when this device has not merged the other device's write before its own, its later stamp still wins the merge and the new token's row stays live; the merge-level fix is lead H115. Was: standalone/reminders.ts:388-397 cancelReminders reads the opt-in, awaits postCancel, then writes { ...optIn, status: 'cancelled' } without reading it again. If another device turns reminders on with a new token meanwhile, the write replaces that active opt-in with the old token cancelled, and the new server row is left with no token in the file. Fix: a sameOptIn re-check after the await, as at :300. Found during PR 1664
